meta.title: Ebola Tracker: DR Congo
meta.description: Independent, sourced tracker of the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak in DR Congo: confirmed cases and deaths, affected provinces, spread to other countries, vaccines, WHO risk and a dated timeline.
meta.disclaimer: This tracker summarises WHO, CDC, ECDC, Africa CDC and national health ministry reports and named news outlets. It is not medical or travel advice. If you develop fever within 21 days of being in an affected area, call a doctor before going to a clinic.

headline: ECDC counts 9,455 confirmed Ebola cases and 4,561 deaths in DR Congo to 17 October, with the outbreak in eight provinces. Kenya has confirmed eight cases.

status.label: Growing · global health emergency
status.summary: The Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak declared on 15 May has now reached 8 of DR Congo's 26 provinces: on 18 October the health ministry confirmed two cases, one fatal, in North Ubangi, AP reported. ECDC's update of 18 October counts 9,455 confirmed cases and 4,561 deaths in DR Congo (data to 17 October), in 66 of 178 health zones across the eight provinces; DR Congo's situation report counted 9,415 cases and 4,536 deaths to 16 October, as reported by Anadolu and Xinhua. CDC calls it the second-largest Ebola outbreak on record. Kenya's health ministry has confirmed eight cases, one of them fatal; three are health workers who cared for the first patient. There is no licensed vaccine for this strain; trials of an existing Ebola vaccine began in August, and an early-phase trial of a Bundibugyo-specific candidate began in Uganda on 6 October.

watch.label: Kenya contact watch
watch.explainer: Ebola's incubation period is 2 to 21 days. Contacts of Kenya's first case were last exposed by 5 October at the latest. Kenya's health ministry confirmed a second case on 14 October, a third on 16 October, four more on 17 October and an eighth on 18 October, all among people already in quarantine, so the follow-up period for their contacts runs later.

claims.claim: There is a vaccine for this Ebola strain
claims.detail: No vaccine is licensed for Bundibugyo virus. Ervebo, licensed for Zaire Ebola, is being tested in trials; whether it protects against Bundibugyo is unknown.

claims.claim: This is the largest Ebola outbreak ever
claims.detail: It is the largest ever in DR Congo and the second-largest on record. The 2014–2016 West Africa outbreak had about 28,600 cases and 11,325 deaths.
CDC reports no confirmed US cases as of 2 October. Two US citizens infected in DR Congo were treated in Germany and recovered.

claims.claim: Ebola spreads through the air like measles or flu
claims.detail: It spreads through direct contact with the body fluids of a sick person or someone who died of it. People are not contagious before they have symptoms.

Kenya has confirmed eight linked cases, one of them fatal. The first, a man who had travelled from DR Congo via Kampala, died on 5 October. The health ministry confirmed further cases from 14 October; on 17 October it reported four more, three of them health workers who cared for the first patient and one a relative, and on 18 October an eighth case, a contact of the first patient who was not a health worker. All were already in quarantine, and officials said there was no evidence of community transmission.
Modelling cited by WHO's Emergency Committee suggests true infections may be three to four times the reported count. Africa CDC says contact tracing reaches only about a quarter of expected contacts.

watchlist.label: US entry restrictions extended
watchlist.note: CDC extended the entry suspension for travellers recently in DR Congo, Uganda or South Sudan by another 30 days on 11 Oct (Nation, Fragomen). Kenya is not on the list.

watchlist.label: US entry restrictions expire unless extended again
watchlist.note: The 11 Oct order runs for 30 days

watchlist.label: Kenya contacts finish 21-day follow-up
watchlist.note: Applies to contacts of the first case. Contacts of the later cases (confirmed 14, 16, 17 and 18 Oct) are followed for 21 days from their last exposure.

watchlist.label: Tumaini vaccine trial begins in DR Congo
watchlist.note: ClinicalTrials.gov lists an estimated start of 20 Oct; CEPI said on 14 Oct that final preparations were underway, and WHO experts expect a start by the end of October, pending approvals. No start had been announced by 20 Oct.

watchlist.label: Official confirmation of cases in North Ubangi
watchlist.note: DR Congo's health ministry confirmed two cases, one fatal, in North Ubangi (AP, 18 Oct); previously reported by Reuters and Bloomberg on 15 Oct

watchlist.label: Next WHO Disease Outbreak News report
watchlist.note: Recent reports came about every two weeks; next not announced

watchlist.label: Third WHO Emergency Committee meeting
watchlist.note: Not announced; recommendations issued 24 Aug normally run three months

watchlist.label: First Bundibugyo-specific vaccine trial begins in Uganda

positions.text: Confirmed an eighth Ebola case, a contact of the first patient who was in quarantine and is not a health worker. The Washington Post reports no community transmission so far.
9,415 confirmed cases and 4,536 deaths to 16 October, with 67 new cases and 26 new deaths in the latest 24-hour report, as reported by Anadolu and Xinhua.

Confirmed four more Ebola cases, bringing the total to seven including the first patient, who died. Three of the four are health workers who cared for the first patient and one is a relative; all were already in quarantine. The ministry said 128 of 130 identified contacts were in quarantine, that there was no evidence of community transmission and that the risk to the general public remained low.

7,890 confirmed cases and 3,799 deaths in 63 health zones across 7 provinces. Risk very high in DR Congo, high for neighbouring countries, low globally. Still a Public Health Emergency of International Concern.
8,787 confirmed cases and 4,242 deaths in DR Congo as of 7 October; the second-largest Ebola outbreak on record. No US cases.
9,066 confirmed cases and 4,381 deaths, as reported by Al Jazeera and Xinhua.
Confirmed Kenya's first imported Bundibugyo case; the patient died. Contacts are being traced and followed.
The outbreak remains a Public Health Emergency of Continental Security, declared on 18 May.

Confirmed a third Ebola case, a close contact of the first two patients who was already in quarantine. The ministry said there was no evidence of community spread and that daily monitoring of contacts continues.

timeline.title: First known case falls ill in Bunia
timeline.body: A health worker who later died in Bunia, Ituri province, is the earliest known case. Investigators believe the outbreak started in the Mongbwalu mining area.

timeline.title: WHO alerted to a deadly unknown illness in Ituri
timeline.body: Reports describe a high-mortality illness in Mongbwalu health zone, including four health workers who died within four days.

timeline.title: DR Congo and Uganda declare a Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak
timeline.body: The national lab confirms Bundibugyo virus. It is DR Congo's 17th Ebola outbreak. Uganda confirms a case in Kampala the same day.

timeline.title: WHO declares a global health emergency
timeline.body: The WHO Director-General declares a Public Health Emergency of International Concern, the first time this was done before convening an Emergency Committee.

timeline.title: Africa CDC declares a continental emergency; US restricts entry
timeline.body: Africa CDC declares a Public Health Emergency of Continental Security. The US suspends entry for foreign nationals recently in DR Congo, Uganda or South Sudan.

timeline.title: US$518 million response plan launched
timeline.body: Africa CDC and WHO launch a joint continental plan covering June to November 2026.

timeline.title: France reports an imported case
timeline.body: An intensive-care doctor returning from DR Congo tests positive in France. He recovers, and none of his contacts fall ill.

timeline.title: First treatment trial for Bundibugyo Ebola begins
timeline.body: The PARTNERS trial enrols its first patient, testing an antibody treatment and remdesivir.

timeline.title: Largest Ebola outbreak in DR Congo's history
timeline.body: With 3,605 confirmed cases in DR Congo, the outbreak passes the 2018–2020 North Kivu outbreak.

timeline.title: WHO keeps the global emergency in place
timeline.body: WHO's Emergency Committee meets for the second time. Modelling it cites suggests true infections may be three to four times the reported count.

timeline.title: Vaccination of health workers begins; Uganda declared Ebola-free
timeline.body: DR Congo starts giving Ervebo, a vaccine licensed for a different Ebola species, to health workers in trials. WHO and Africa CDC confirm the end of Uganda's outbreak after 42 days without cases.

timeline.title: Outbreak reaches a seventh province, Sud-Ubangi
timeline.body: A death in Bulu health zone marks the first spread to western DR Congo.

timeline.title: Frontline worker vaccine study launched in Bunia
timeline.body: MSF's BRAVO study plans to vaccinate about 20,000 frontline workers in Ituri and North Kivu.

timeline.title: WHO: 7,890 cases, 3,799 deaths in 63 health zones
timeline.body: The outbreak has reached Dungu health zone, on the border with South Sudan. WHO rates the risk very high in DR Congo and high for neighbouring countries.

timeline.title: G20 pledges more than US$470 million
timeline.body: New pledges at the G20 foreign ministers' meeting include US$267 million from the US.

timeline.title: MSF health worker evacuated to the Netherlands
timeline.body: A Medecins Sans Frontieres staff member infected in DR Congo is admitted to Leiden University Medical Center.

timeline.title: CDC: 8,442 cases and 4,080 deaths
timeline.body: CDC calls it the second-largest Ebola outbreak on record and says it is spreading faster than earlier ones. No cases in the US.

timeline.title: Kenya's first imported case dies in Nairobi
timeline.body: A Kenyan citizen living in DR Congo travelled by road to Kampala and flew to Nairobi on 3 October. He tested positive and died on 5 October. Contacts are being followed.

timeline.title: CDC and ECDC: 8,603 cases and 4,148 deaths
timeline.body: DR Congo's confirmed total reaches 8,603 cases, including 4,148 deaths, with data to 4 October. ECDC notes that DR Congo's figures are under continuous review and may be revised.

timeline.title: ECDC: 8,728 cases and 4,205 deaths
timeline.body: ECDC's update of 7 October, with data to 6 October, reports DR Congo's confirmed total at 8,728 cases, including 4,205 deaths. Ituri has 6,513 cases and North Kivu 1,785. ECDC notes that DR Congo's figures are under continuous review and may be revised.

timeline.title: Bundibugyo vaccine trial begins in Uganda
timeline.body: The MRC/UVRI & LSHTM Uganda Research Unit vaccinated the first participants in Masaka City with a candidate vaccine developed by the University of Oxford. The early-phase study tests safety and immune response in healthy adults and follows a trial of the same candidate in the UK. It does not yet show whether the vaccine protects against the virus.

timeline.title: CDC: 8,787 cases and 4,242 deaths
timeline.body: CDC's situation summary counts 8,787 confirmed cases and 4,242 confirmed deaths in DR Congo as of 7 October. DR Congo's health ministry does not include probable cases in its official reporting.

timeline.title: DR Congo reports 9,066 cases and 4,381 deaths
timeline.body: DR Congo's health ministry reported 9,066 confirmed Ebola cases and 4,381 deaths in its update of 13 October, according to Al Jazeera and Xinhua. Media reports describe it as the country's largest and deadliest Ebola outbreak. Ituri province accounts for most confirmed cases.

timeline.title: WHO experts: Tumaini vaccine trial expected by end of October
timeline.body: WHO experts said the Tumaini trial in DR Congo is expected to begin by the end of October. It will first test Ervebo, which is licensed for the Zaire strain, to see whether it protects against Bundibugyo virus. Candidates from Oxford and Moderna, now in early-phase trials, may be added later. Whether Ervebo protects against this strain is not yet known.

timeline.title: Kenya confirms a second Ebola case
timeline.body: Kenya's health ministry said a relative of the first patient, who was already in quarantine and under daily monitoring, tested positive after developing symptoms on 13 October. The ministry said it identified 128 contacts of the first patient and found no evidence of spread in the community. Kenya now has two confirmed cases and one death.

timeline.title: ECDC and CDC: 9,144 cases and 4,410 deaths
timeline.body: ECDC reports 9,144 confirmed cases and 4,410 deaths in DR Congo as of 13 October (data to 12 October), with 899 patients in isolation in hospital and 65 of 167 health zones affected across 7 provinces. CDC's situation summary of 14 October lists the same DR Congo totals and 2 confirmed cases and 1 death in Kenya.

timeline.title: Africa CDC asks for accountability on over $700 million of response funding
timeline.body: Africa CDC's director general said on 14 October that more than $700 million of Ebola response funding channelled through international partners could not yet be traced to the response, and that the funds were not transferred to the DR Congo government. He asked partners to account for the money, and DR Congo authorities said they would ask the partners concerned for explanations.

timeline.title: Media report Ebola in an eighth province, North Ubangi
timeline.body: Reuters and Bloomberg report, citing health officials, two confirmed Ebola cases in North Ubangi province, which borders the Central African Republic. Reuters says Congolese authorities had not yet officially announced the cases. It also reports that several suspected Ebola deaths had recently occurred at a mining site in Wapinda health zone, with samples sent for laboratory analysis in the province and in Kinshasa.

timeline.title: ECDC: 9,277 cases and 4,478 deaths
timeline.body: ECDC reports 9,277 confirmed cases and 4,478 deaths in DR Congo as of 15 October (data to 14 October), with 924 patients in isolation in hospital. New cases in the latest report were in Ituri (31), North Kivu (28), Haut-Uele (5) and Tshopo (1). ECDC also notes the media reports of cases in North Ubangi.

timeline.title: Kenya confirms a third Ebola case
timeline.body: Kenya's health ministry said a close contact of the first two patients, who had been in quarantine since 6 October, tested positive. The ministry said there was no evidence of community spread, and contacts continue daily monitoring for 21 days. Kenya now has three confirmed cases and one death.

timeline.title: DR Congo reports 9,415 cases and 4,536 deaths
timeline.body: DR Congo's latest situation report counts 9,415 confirmed cases and 4,536 deaths since the outbreak began, including 67 new cases and 26 new deaths in the 24 hours to 16 October, Anadolu and Xinhua report.

timeline.title: Kenya confirms four more Ebola cases, total seven
timeline.body: Kenya's health ministry said four more people tested positive, bringing the total to seven including the first patient, who died. Three are health workers who cared for the first patient and one is a relative; all were already in quarantine. The ministry said 128 of 130 identified contacts were in quarantine, that there was no evidence of community transmission and that the risk to the general public remained low.

timeline.title: Kenya confirms an eighth Ebola case
timeline.body: Kenya's health ministry said one more person tested positive, bringing the total to eight including the first patient, who died. The new case is a contact of the first patient who was in quarantine; the ministry said he is not a health worker. The Washington Post reports no community transmission so far.

timeline.title: DR Congo confirms Ebola in an eighth province, North Ubangi
timeline.body: DR Congo's health ministry said on 18 October that the outbreak has reached North Ubangi province, which borders the Central African Republic, with two cases, one of them fatal, in Wapinda health zone. Reuters and Bloomberg had reported the cases on 15 October before the official statement. AP reports the outbreak has recorded at least 9,400 confirmed cases and more than 4,500 deaths, with Ituri province accounting for almost three quarters of cases.

timeline.title: ECDC counts 9,455 cases and 4,561 deaths
timeline.body: ECDC's update, with data to 17 October, counts 9,455 confirmed cases and 4,561 deaths in DR Congo, with 925 patients in isolation and 2,530 recoveries. It reports 66 of 178 health zones affected across eight provinces, and notes that DR Congo's figures are under continuous review and harmonisation, so they may change.

history.text: Bundibugyo virus is first identified in Bundibugyo District, Uganda: 131 cases and 42 deaths.
Second known outbreak, around Isiro in north-eastern DR Congo.
The largest Bundibugyo outbreak by far: more than 9,000 confirmed cases in DR Congo, plus cases in Uganda, France and Kenya.

facts.a: Through direct contact with the blood or body fluids of a person who is sick with or has died from Ebola, or with contaminated objects. It does not spread through the air, and people are not contagious before symptoms start.
Fever, fatigue, muscle pain, headache and sore throat, followed by vomiting, diarrhoea, rash and in some cases bleeding. Symptoms appear 2 to 21 days after infection, usually within 4 to 10.
There is no licensed treatment for Bundibugyo virus. Early supportive care improves survival. A trial testing an antibody treatment and remdesivir began in July 2026.
Not for this strain. Ervebo protects against Zaire Ebola; trials in DR Congo are testing whether it helps against Bundibugyo, starting with health and frontline workers.
It is one of several Ebola virus species, named after the district in Uganda where it was first identified in 2007. Fruit bats are the suspected natural host.
